about: The root-cause clusters of the accessibility findings ledger (lib/a11y-issues.mjs; tests/AGENTS.md, A11y: the findings ledger and the cluster catalog). A cluster has id, title, an optional tracker (a task id, or a list of them; code, never printed on the page) or an optional notDefect (the class that says why its findings are not a defect, never beside a tracker), and match rules: source, then any of checks, kinds, rules, causes, criteria, pages, themes, where, axeIssues. Values in a field are ORed, fields in a rule ANDed, rules in a cluster ORed. A where pattern reads the finding's masked selector, its step, or both joined as '<masked selector> @ <step>'. A finding no rule matches lands in needs-triage; one that two rules match fails lib/__tests__/a11y-issues.test.mjs. triage lists every sampled finding shape (findingShape()) left in needs-triage, each with why it is neither a known cause nor the reader's own behavior yet; its length is the triage limit, exact: a shape leaves the list when it is sorted into a cluster, and joins it only visibly, with its reason, in the change that adds it.

clusters.title: The overlay clones split the accessibility tree: the column headers read after the data, each row is exposed twice, the row headers sit apart from their rows, and a screen reader loses the cell's row index (VoiceOver with Chromium names a cell's column one lower)
Reading mode skips a row at the edge of the rendered band of a long grid (A5 of 200 rows), on every reader but NVDA with Chromium
In reading mode NVDA with Chromium stops on an empty item (`blank`) right before the grid, so the reading cursor reaches nothing where the table should start
With Chromium a jump to a row the grid renders only once it scrolls there (Ctrl+ArrowDown to the last of 200 rows) is not announced
The grid is built from divs with ARIA roles, and its treegrid root holds children the role does not allow

The focus is not returned to the cell after Escape, Enter, Tab or a shortcut closes an editor, a menu or the comment editor, or an arrow key closes a submenu: it stays on the closed editor's field or falls to the document, and a screen reader does not announce the cell or the parent item

An editor's list does not announce the choice the keys reach: with Chromium the autocomplete and dropdown options that aria-activedescendant names have no name, a narrowed list and its highlighted choice are silent on every reader, and the handsontable editor exposes no highlighted row at all

With imeFastEdit the browser focus sits in the editor's hidden input while a cell is only selected, so a date or time cell reads as that input (`Year, spin button, 2024`, `6 month stepper`) or not at all, VoiceOver differently from run to run, and Enter, which opens the editor without a focus move, is silent on NVDA with Firefox
The autocomplete and dropdown editors put the combobox role on a textarea, which ARIA in HTML does not allow, and name a closed list in aria-controls that axe cannot find

VoiceOver with WebKit reads a text field the focus moves to inside the grid, a menu or the sheets bar by its value or label alone, without its role (the cell editors, the filter inputs, the sheet rename field), where it names the role of a field outside them

Controls without an accessible name or role: the filter condition select and the filter listbox, the autocomplete list, the focus catchers a menu leaves armed, the editor inputs on the website until it ships the release that names them, and the comment editor's reader announcement

The two hidden focus catchers stay armed while the focus is on body (the sheets bar page, where the element that held it went away), because a Tab from the browser UI sends no keydown and only an armed catcher lets it re-enter the grid; they carry no role on purpose, so a screen reader is not sent to a hidden stop

The empty data state's message, for no data and for loading, takes the focus as a div with no role, so NVDA with Firefox reads `section` without its text and VoiceOver with WebKit reads its title alone

The formula builder's editor puts the combobox role on a textarea, which ARIA in HTML does not allow, and names a closed list in aria-controls: VoiceOver reads only the typed text, neither the suggestion that typing highlights nor the function help the editor names as its description, and with WebKit an empty list (`0 items`); and its options' ids follow their place in the list, so when typing refilters it and the active option stays first, aria-activedescendant keeps its value and NVDA with Chromium says nothing (NVDA with Firefox reads the new option)
The formula builder's function help panel takes the focus as a div with no role, and Tab does not leave it
The formula builder's error cell points aria-errormessage at its error popup, a tooltip with no live region, which axe rejects
Moving the focus onto the formula editor with Tab or Shift+Tab changes the context, which a focus move alone must not do
Tab in the formula editor accepts the highlighted suggestion and keeps the focus in the editor, as the formula builder intends: the keyboard walker reads it as a Tab that stays
A cell that holds a formula reads as its result alone: nothing the cell exposes says that it holds a formula
A screen reader hears the context and column menus as a table, NVDA without the word menu, and VoiceOver's next item (VO+Right) moves along the table's row and out of the menu

A checkbox in a cell or a header does not announce its state: the focus stays on the cell, so the mixed state of the check all and select all checkboxes and a row header checkbox's state are never read, the corner reads its own name over the select all checkbox, and Space toggling one is silent with Chromium
A read-only cell is not announced as read only: the cell carries aria-readonly, which no reader says when the focus reaches it
A link in a cell is not announced as a link: the focus stays on the cell, whose name is its text, and the link inside never takes the focus, so NVDA reads the address and never says link
What a plugin marks on a cell with a class alone is not announced: a commented cell and a column summary cell read as plain cells, the read-only summary without its read-only state
A merged cell's span is not read by NVDA with Firefox or by VoiceOver, though the cell carries rowspan and colspan: only NVDA with Chromium says `through row 3 column 3`
The accessible name of the Filters "Filter by value" component does not include its visible text
Text, icon, checkbox, grid line, selection and focus indicator contrast under 4.5:1 or 3:1 per theme
Drags without a single-pointer or keyboard alternative, and controls that act on the press or after the pointer left
Content cut off or pushed out of view at 320 px or 200 %, hover content that does not dismiss, and motion that runs on or ignores the reduced-motion preference
The loading dialog's spinner turns for as long as the load lasts: 2.2.2 exempts it, because nothing else can be done while it shows
In forced colors the highlighted menu item or the header icons are not drawn

A range extension, Ctrl+A selecting every cell, the place in the order of a column added to a multi-column sort, and a nested row's level are not announced: no status message reaches the screen reader. The level is announced since #14355, and NVDA reads it; the VoiceOver rows of those steps have a cluster of their own

On VoiceOver the nested rows level message (`Level 1, 1 of 38`) replaces the cell's own announcement when the focus reaches another row, so the cell's value is not read: with WebKit on the nested rows page in every run and on the complex demo in one run of two (the audit of 2026-11-23 heard the message alone, the recording run after it the cell and then the message), with Chromium on the move into a frozen row; NVDA reads both

A load that starts or ends without a focus move is not announced: a sheet switch that starts a server fetch (the loading message is no live region), and a pending cell's value that arrives (with Chromium)

A screen reader does not read a focused cell that changes in place: VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing for a checkbox or the check all box toggled, a Filter by value item unchecked, a pending value that arrives, and the jump to the last row of a long grid, which draws the last cell where the focus already is; NVDA with Firefox reads only the new value there, without its row. The cell keeps its accessibility object now that its attributes are written only when they change, so the readers take the change for an update of the cell they are on, not a move
A pending or failed cell's visually hidden status text follows its value with no space between them, so VoiceOver with WebKit reads the two as one word (`Old BLoading...`) and neither on its own

VoiceOver does not read a freeze bar's frozen count: the bars carry aria-valuenow over a range and no aria-valuetext (left out for want of a plural form per language), so a move reads as a percentage and a focus as a splitter without its count

VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing when Enter expands a collapsed column group, though it reads the collapse; a plain header put through the same redraw is read both ways, so the silence comes from the grid

VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing when Enter commits the password editor and moves the focus to the next cell; it reads the focus leaving a plain password field and the select editor's commit to a cell, so the silence comes from the grid
axe's experimental focus-order-semantics rule lists the freeze bars for review: a focusable separator is the window splitter pattern, which the rule does not take as a widget
Tab walks out of an open modal dialog to the content behind it, which the dialog hides from assistive technology
Links and checkboxes are smaller than 24 by 24 px, or sit closer than that to their neighbors

VoiceOver names no row number on a cell move, no column number in WebKit and no header role on a header, on a well-formed grid too: the screen reader's behavior, not the grid's (the scenario notes record it)

VoiceOver says checked for a checked menu item and nothing for an unchecked one, on a well-formed menu too: the screen reader's behavior, not the grid's (the Read only item reads checked once its column is read only)
When the arrow key opens a submenu (ArrowRight, or ArrowLeft right to left), VoiceOver reads the parent item (`Alignment expanded`), not the submenu item that takes the focus

VoiceOver, with Chromium and with WebKit, does not read the message a formula error cell carries in aria-description (`Function name NOPE not recognized.`): it says the error value and that the data is invalid, where NVDA reads the message too

VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing when the keys change the option of a closed select, on a plain select too, whether a script changes it as the select editor does or its own type-ahead does: the screen reader's behavior, not the grid's

VoiceOver with WebKit does not follow the focus when Tab leaves the grid for a link after it (the license notice's links, the Powered by badge): it says nothing or reads the link focused before, and its reading cursor stays in the grid, so reading on reads cells, not the notice

A screen reader says nothing on a step whose surface it reads on later steps or in other runs: VoiceOver on the first key after the runner enters the page above all, on cells, headers, menus, editors and page buttons alike, which points at the reader's start-up, not at the surface; a golden difference belongs here only where this run was the silent one

An announcement or an accessibility tree differs from its golden with no defect behind it: reader wording that varies between runs (the echo of typed characters catches more or fewer of them, a status message can cut short what VoiceOver reads before it, and VoiceOver with WebKit names a menu item's group one way or another), a golden that recorded a start-up silence the run did not repeat, and a reading golden recorded a phrase late; record the golden again
